podcast.body: The self-titled debut album from Bowie's grungy rock band, featuring a metallic, feedback-laden sound that was noisier than anything he had attempted before, as a response to art punk bands like Pixies and Sonic Youth. While the lead track "Under the God" did well on the modern rock chart, the album only peaked at number 28 and did not go gold, struggling to establish the band beyond Bowie's side project status. "He released a self-titled album filled with noisy rock."

podcast.body: This self-titled album was the debut of the four-piece rock band Tin Machine, formed by Bowie as its lead singer. The band drew inspiration from artists like Jimi Hendrix, Cream, and the Pixies, and their sound was distinctly different from earlier David Bowie records. It received harsh reviews, with some critics viewing Bowie as an "old man trying to be hip again." "Tin Machine from their self-titled Davy album and a single entitled Under the God."
